text:
amanda_sales: FYI — TidalPay wants to run a 4-week POC to migrate from VendorX to Redwood. Key asks: API parity (prompt/response diffs), pricing delta, SSO/KMS requirements, and enterprise security questionnaire. Kickoff meeting tomorrow 10am PT. Can engineering + security confirm what we need to show?

jia_engineer: I can lead the parity side. Do we have a canonical set of sample prompts & expected outputs from VendorX? We'll need those to run side-by-side A/Bs.

amanda_sales: @jia_engineer they shared a small batch of 12 prompts; attached in the email I sent. Also asked about streaming vs non-streaming behavior and stop-token handling.

omar_se: For streaming, Redwood supports chunked streaming with prefix caching. Differences we should highlight: vendorX used trailing newlines as implicit stops; we enforce explicit stop sequences unless passing stop: null. Quick snippet to reproduce VendorX behavior:

```json
POST /v1/generate
Content-Type: application/json
{
  "prompt": "Summarize: ...",
  "stream": true,
  "stop": ["\n\n"]
}
```

We should run that against both endpoints and capture token boundaries.

priyanka_ml: On output deltas — quantify with ROUGE/BLEU + custom predicate checks for required entities (payment_token, account_mask). Also test temperature/seed behavior; VendorX returns slightly different deterministic outputs despite same seed in their infra — need to call that out.

amanda_sales: TidalPay also asked about rate limits and per-customer billing. Pricing question: can we give them an estimate per 1M txns/day with 128 token avg?

eli_sre: For pricing, we usually map to token compute + concurrency tier. Quick estimate: 1M requests/day * 128 avg tokens = 128M tokens/day. If they need 99th percentile latency <150ms we recommend Dedicated small pool or a Reserved slot. I'll draft a cost band and put numbers in the shared sheet.

amanda_sales: Thx. Security: they require SSO (SAML), customer-managed keys for encryption at rest (KMS/HSM), SOC2 + penetration testing evidence, and an encryption in transit cert rotation policy. Can security confirm we can satisfy?

secbot: Automated check: Redwood supports SAML SSO integrations (Okta, OneLogin), KMS integrations (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, BYOK/HSM via API), SOC2 Type II on record, and quarterly pen-tests. I will attach the most recent audit artifacts link in #sec-docs.

elena_legal: Note: They asked for a data residency clause (EU only) and a 6-month data deletion SLA. We'll need to review contract language and CISO contact. Also list of subprocessors required.

omar_se: Practical POC plan suggestion:
1) Baseline: run the 12 prompts against VendorX and Redwood hosted (same model family in our catalog).
2) Instrument: capture token-level traces, latencies, and deterministic seeds.
3) Parity tests: entity presence checks, stop token divergences, and sampling variance stats.
4) Regression: run 500-sample run across prompt variants and compare metrics.

jia_engineer: I'll spin up a small test harness. Need staging API keys + IP allowlist for their smoke tests. Amanda — can you get the staging CIDR and contact?

amanda_sales: Yep. TidalPay provided staging IPs: 34.123.45.210/32 and 34.123.45.211/32. I'll add to the sheet. Also they requested a temporary SLA (uptime for POC). We can offer 99.5% for the window.

eli_sre: Add-on: we'll enable request-level logs and redact PII by default. For KMS testing, we can create a test-key and give them a rotated keyflow exercise. Expect ~48h to provision.

priyanka_ml: For prompt parity, also include temperature sweep (0.0, 0.2, 0.7) and top_p tests. Document sampling variance with seed where possible. I'll provide the eval harness and expected scoring notebook.

amanda_sales: Great — looks like action items: 1) @jia_engineer build harness and run baseline by EOD Wed. 2) @eli_sre provision staging keys/IPs + temporary SLA doc. 3) @secbot post audit artifacts + confirm BYOK steps. 4) @elena_legal draft data residency + subprocessor clause. 5) I'll coordinate pricing band and draft the POC statement of work.

elena_legal: Will do, will ping CISO for review.

omar_se: One blocker to flag for the meeting: VendorX uses a nonstandard metadata header X-Vendor-Context that influences decoding; if TidalPay relied on that we'll need to map it to our request.metadata field or implement a shim. Please ask them to surface any such headers during kickoff.

amanda_sales: Noted — I'll ask them to list any custom headers. Meeting invite sent (10am PT). Please bring any short demos you want to show. :thumbsup:
